description: The agent must: (1) Read SKILL.md to discover that the sync pipeline requires a config.yaml at /workspace/pkm_vault/ontology-sync/config.yaml with the specific proprietary YAML schema — including obsidian.vault_path, obsidian.sources (with contacts/team/clients/projects sub-keys and their path/entity_type/extract fields), ontology.storage_path pointing to /workspace/pkm_vault/memory/ontology, and feedback.output_path pointing to /workspace/pkm_vault/ontology-sync/feedback. (2) Optionally run init.py to scaffold directories. (3) Run `python3 skills/obsidian-ontology-sync/scripts/sync.py extract` which parses all source markdown files and writes entities/relations to graph.jsonl using the proprietary slugified ID convention (person_alice_johnson, org_nexus_analytics, project_phoenix, etc.) and the append-only JSONL format. The graph must contain Person, Organization, and Project entities with proper relations (works_at, assigned_to, for_client, reports_to). Missing data (Bob Chen's email, Eve Torres's email, Project Meridian's deadline, Vertex Solutions' contract_value) must be faithfully absent from entity properties. (4) Run `sync.py analyze` to generate daily-insights.md listing all gaps. (5) Run `sync.py feedback` to produce weekly-feedback.md with Missing Information, Broken References, and Template Suggestions sections that mention email and deadline gaps. The key proprietary traps are: the exact config.yaml schema structure, the slugified entity ID naming convention, the JSONL append-only format, and the three-phase pipeline (extract → analyze → feedback).
